data.body:
INSTRUMENTED CONFIRMATION — the 14-minute gap is a reporting artifact, and both alternative branches are refuted by measurement.

EXPERIMENT. Two scratch files under a throwaway tests/unit/scratch_0078/ (removed after the run; nothing committed):
- test_zz_gap_blocked.py — a test that parks in a blocking Popen.communicate() read on a child's pipes, i.e. exactly the shape _convert is in while pandoc runs.
- test_aa_gap_slow.py — 24 short passing tests (5s each) that keep the session alive after the other worker dies.
Run as: pytest tests/unit/scratch_0078 -q -n 2 --dist loadfile --timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread, with every output line timestamped relative to session start.

RESULT 1 — the timeout DOES fire on this path, promptly. The test blocked inside the subprocess pipe read was killed at t+20.52s against a 20s budget. pytest-timeout's thread method runs its timer in a separate thread and calls os._exit(1), which needs no cooperation from the thread parked in the read. So 'the timeout is not firing because the pandoc subprocess is not interruptible' is refuted: it fires at the budget, to within half a second.

RESULT 2 — the gap between the two log lines is remaining-session time, not kill latency. First 'node down: Not properly terminated' at t+20.52s; the "worker 'gwN' crashed while running ..." lines printed at t+278.48s. That is a 258-SECOND gap against a 20-SECOND budget — 12.9x — produced entirely by the surviving worker finishing its short tests. Same structure as CI's 14 minutes against 300s.

The source explains why. The two lines come from different places at different times:
- xdist/workermanage.py:407 logs 'node down' LIVE, at the moment the worker dies.
- xdist/dsession.py:436 (handle_crashitem) builds an ordinary pytest.TestReport(outcome='failed', longrepr=msg), and pytest prints failure reports in the FAILURES section at SESSION END.
So the premise 'if the per-test timeout were firing cleanly the gap should be ~5 minutes' does not hold — the gap measures how much suite remained after the crash, and carries no information about the kill. CI's arithmetic fits: session 1602.64s (26.7 min), crash ~12.7 min in, 14 min of suite left.

(Incidental, and it explains why one crashing test burns so much wall clock: xdist REPLACES a crashed worker, the replacement re-runs the same poisoned test and dies too. The scratch run cycled through gw1..gw9 that way.)

RESULT 3 — not OOM. Peak RSS for a process running the entire corpus comparison is 92.6 MB (/usr/bin/time -l). The macOS runner has ~7 GB and CI runs 3 workers. The test holds ~884 short strings and spawns ONE pandoc at a time, so there is no memory pressure anywhere near a kill. Refuted.

CONCLUSION: single confirmed cause — the test's unbounded serial cost (91.6s idle, 504.8s saturated) crosses CI's 300s per-test guard on the contended macOS lane, and --timeout-method=thread converts that into a worker kill with no traceback rather than a test failure.

FIX VERIFIED (change 1745, commit 3e8325559a).
- Worst single case: 91.6s -> 4.37s idle; 504.8s -> 38.05s under the identical 2x hw.ncpu saturation (7.9x headroom under the 300s guard).
- Full CI invocation 'pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread': 12857 passed, 60 skipped, 0 failed, no worker crash; the test no longer appears in the slowest 8.
- tests/integration: 194 passed, 1 skipped.
- Coverage guard proven to fail RED: temporarily dropping a chunk made test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit fail, then reverted.
- All 884 units still compared, _EQUIVALENCE_STRIDE still 1, real pandoc on both sides. No timeout raise, no retry marker, no elapsed-time assertion.
